wordHints.Time: Time is a well-known news magazine, providing weekly coverage of current events, politics, and culture.
wordHints.The Economist: The Economist is a global magazine that covers economics, current affairs, and business from a global perspective.
wordHints.Cosmopolitan: Cosmopolitan is a women's lifestyle magazine that focuses on fashion, beauty, relationships, and celebrity culture.
wordHints.National Geographic: National Geographic is known for its photography and articles about world cultures, geography, history, and science.
wordHints.Reader’s Digest: Reader's Digest is a general interest magazine known for its condensed articles, anecdotes, and humor, aimed at a broad audience.

fullAnalysis: At first glance, Time, The Economist, Cosmopolitan do not suggest one clean pattern. The board only tightens once a later clue makes the shared category feel much more specific. That is why guesses like "New York" and "Informative" can feel plausible at the start. The clue that changes the frame is "Cosmopolitan".

From there, These publications boast wide circulation and varied content for diverse audiences explains the board more cleanly than broader labels. Once that frame clicks, entries like A popular news magazine, A global business magazine, A women's lifestyle magazine stop feeling scattered and start feeling like members of the same family. The clues are diverse in subject matter, obscuring their common format. The brands are so well-known that solvers might not think about the higher category.

I did not have a clean category from the first clue. I initially drifted toward Newspapers, which felt plausible for a moment, but while some newspapers have national reach, the clues are more focused on general interest, lifestyle, and visual content, unlike standard news reporting.

The turn came when I let cosmopolitan lead the solve instead of treating it like an outlier. Once I read the board through these publications boast wide circulation and varied content for diverse audiences, clues that had seemed broad started feeling like members of the same category, especially A popular news magazine and A global business magazine. At that point, the final connector was the only reading that explained the full set without stretching anything.

lessons.title: Broad clues can create the wrong frame early
lessons.body: When the first clues are very open-ended, it is often better to wait for a more specific word before locking in a category.

lessons.title: The narrowing clue matters more than the loudest clue
lessons.body: Cosmopolitan is what organizes this board. Once one clue produces a precise natural reading, re-check the earlier clues under that same frame.

lessons.title: Prefer precise category fit over broad topic logic
lessons.body: Consider the type of source material. Is it a book, periodical, website, or something else?
